classification.difficultyReason: Development: connect the unnecessarily large £0–£200 range with suppressed visible price differences, then propose finer intervals and a lower maximum while preserving the taught zero baseline for bars.

content.prompt: The price of the same basket of groceries was compared at 5 supermarkets. Prices are in pounds (£).

spec.description: Source coarse scale £0,£100,£200 retained; relative bar heights reconstructed approximately from source. No exact prices asserted.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why the chart is misleading.

answer.short: The £0–£200 range makes the price differences hard to see.
answer.worked: All bars are below £100, but the scale extends to £200. This compresses their heights and makes price differences hard to compare.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Describe how the chart could be improved.

answer.short: Keep zero as the baseline and use a maximum of £100, with finer ticks.
answer.worked: Use a vertical scale from £0 to £100 with smaller intervals. Keep equal-width bars and the zero baseline so their heights remain proportional to prices.
